text:
The Kings might be the unluckiest team in hockey right now, and the standings don't care. Los Angeles is 5-11-2 with 12 points and winless in four (0-4-0), outscored 16-6, even though it took 54% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) in those games. Over the season it has taken 52% of the five-on-five chances. Our points model has them about eight points behind what their play has earned.

Most of the gap is in net. Darcy Kuemper played his 500th NHL game this week, a real milestone, but he is at .847 and 6.4 goals worse than expected over his last five starts, and the team has allowed almost nine more goals than its chances. The shooters haven't helped, finishing 7.5 goals below their chances.

There's plenty that works. Adrian Kempe, Artemi Panarin and Alex Laferriere have taken 61% of the chances and outscored teams 8-3. Brandt Clarke with Erik Gustafsson drives play from the back. Kevin Fiala is back after a long absence and picked up a power-play assist in his first game.

Peter Laviolette's team still has 25% playoff odds by our numbers, which says how much is left if the saves come. Panarin missed a game for family reasons. What we'd watch: Kuemper's next few starts, because the season probably turns on them.
